mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in a single month reduces near-term discount rates, lowering the present value of expected equity cash flows and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in the same month are not statistically lower than the prior month's average (t-test p > 0.05), or the shock is not confirmed by a persistent rise in yields.

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in CPIAUCSL exceeds +0.6%, it indicates accelerating inflation expectations, which compresses the real return on equities and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in the subsequent quarter are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the 12-month inflation rate does not exceed +0.6%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in PAYEMS of at least 3% for three consecutive months signals strengthening labor market momentum, which raises consumer confidence and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥3% month-over-month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the labor momentum pattern is not sustained beyond the 3-month window.

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 (billions of chained USD) grows by more than 10% in a quarter, it indicates robust corporate and consumer demand, which supports equity valuation expansion and yields positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in the following quarter are not significantly higher than the prior quarter's average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in INDPRO (monthly index) of at least 5 points for two months suggests weakening industrial production capacity, which raises uncertainty and compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by ≥5 points for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in the month following the contraction are not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in HOUST (units) and RSAFS (dollars) by at least 5% and 8% respectively in the same month indicate robust industrial and retail demand, which elevates earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST ↑ ≥5% AND RSAFS ↑ ≥8% in the same month
regime_hint: Dual industrial and retail demand acceleration
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the interaction pattern is not confirmed in at least 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 3.5% for two consecutive months, it suggests easing labor market pressure and reduced wage growth expectations, which can reduce equity risk premia and support positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05) or UNRATE does not remain below 3.5% for the full horizon.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of monetary easing (as signaled by FEDFUNDS < 4.0%), the 2-month moving average of CPIAUCSL shows a downward trend of at least 0.2%, which lowers real rates and supports equity price appreciation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the FEDFUNDS/CPIAUCSL relationship breaks down in subsequent months.
